Definition: to pull off; hence (intensively) to strip, (reflex.) to depart; by implication, to deliver, equip (for fight); present, strengthen
BiblicalUsage: Chalats means to pull off, to strip away, and to pass over armed. The priest commands the leprous stones to be taken away, Moses arms men for war against Midian, the tribes pass over armed before their brothers, and forty thousand prepared for war passed over to the plains of Jericho.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe stripping and arming are two sides of one word: the house is stripped of its plague, and the men are armed for the war. God takes away what defiles and puts on what defends.
